name: Hotaru
greeting:
A small light hovers beside the bed, its wings trembling.

There you are, {player}. I’m Hotaru. I’ll stay with you. Before we go anywhere, let me hear your voice.
prompt: We can take this one step at a time. What would you like to try?

topics.title: How do I say hello?
lines: Your lips move, but no words come yet. That’s all right. We’ll start with something small.
I’ve opened a place in your Field Notes for your first program. Put Hello, Hotaru! inside print, with quotation marks around the words. Test lets you listen first. Speak lets me hear you.

lesson.title: Field Notes / 00 · Saying Hello
lesson.explanation: print sends text out of your program. In your first morning, the words also become a proposed voice. Test, then Speak.

topics.title: What comes after hello?
lines: Hello. There’s your voice. Hotaru’s wings give a quick flutter. Now let’s give those feet a little direction. One press, one step.
Your next page is First Steps. Each key starts at x = y = 0. Add one to y to step north, or one to x to step east. You can watch what happens in the little room before trying it here.
We’ll open that page now. Test a block with its arrow, or Test code to check the whole program. Apply connects the keys. Then Continue brings you back to me to practise.

lesson.title: Field Notes / 01 · Your first steps
lesson.source:
def program(world):
    x = y = 0
    y += 1
    world.controls.bind_move("W", x, y)
lesson.explanation: A key event begins at zero, adds a movement and records that binding. Only one cardinal step can be applied. Add the other three directions in your notes.

topics.title: Will you come with me?
lines: Of course. I’ll keep close. If you lose your way, speak to me again.
There’s no hurry to finish the whole village today. A voice and a few steady steps are a good beginning.

topics.title: What should I do in the hollow?
lines: The lamps have gone quiet. Mira is nearby; she knows this village better than either of us.
Walk with WASD or click a place. Your notebook opens with E. Test a small change, look at its preview, then Apply when you’re ready. I’ll keep you company.
